title: Protocol for image registration of correlative soft X-ray tomography and super-resolution structured illumination microscopy images
protocol: Add the SIR data (for 2-channel data files) to both the reference and target fields in Chromagnon.
Alternatively, if each fluorescence channel is available in separate files, add one as the ‘target’ and one as the ‘source’.
Press ‘Run all’.
Evaluate the result visually; fluorescence signal should align well in all dimensions.
Obtain reference files from the microscope facility/beamline support scientists.
Choose the appropriate ‘chromagnon.csv’ reference file that matches the laser wavelength and filter used for imaging your sample.
Add the chosen reference file to the ‘reference’ field.
Add the SIR data to be aligned in the ‘source’ field.
Set the suffix to be used in the target panel as .dv for output format.
Press ‘Run all’ to process the alignment.
Evaluate the result visually; ensure that fluorescence signal aligns well.
For batch-processing, place all SIR images to be aligned in the source field.
Add the reference file in the reference field.
Press ‘Run all’ to process multiple images at once.
Acquire pairs of images, with one common channel in both pairs.
Designate one image from one channel as the reference for all transformations.
Perform chromatic shift correction on each channel.
Open Icy.
Open datasets of the same channel taken at different times.
Calculate stage shift and apply matrix to correct for stage shift to other channels.
Open ec-CLEM.
Assign the images as ‘target’ (the reference image) and ‘source’ (the image that you want to transform).
Follow steps d-h from the Image Registration section of this paper to co-register the images.
Save the transformation schema file in the source image folder.
Open the data corresponding to the second channel from ‘source’ <filename>._SIR_ALN.dv.
In ec-CLEM, go to ‘Advanced Usage’→ ‘Apply transformation matrix’.
Choose the channel to transform and the transformation schema file that was just created.
Click the play button to apply the transform.
Save the transformed data.
Repeat the steps if there are other images that require alignment for stage shift.
Merge all final aligned channels into one image using Icy (Sequence→Merge) or ImageJ/Fiji.
Choose minimum as the projection type for the bright-field image stack and the X-ray tomogram stacks.
Manually adjust the contrast using the minimum and maximum sliders on the histogram in Icy.
Save these projection images to use in the next steps.
Open Fiji and go to Image→ Stacks → Z Project.
For the SIR stack, choose ‘maximum intensity’ for the projection type.
For the bright-field image stack and the X-ray tomogram stacks, choose ‘minimum intensity’ for the projection type.
Manually adjust the contrast if needed by going to Image→Adjust→Brightness/Contrast.
Name and save these projection images.
Compute the 2D image registrations.
Ensure 2D SIR, 2D brightfield, and 2D X-ray images are saved in the same directory.
Open Icy and an image pair from each row shown in Table 2.
Check that the metadata, such as pixel size and image dimensions, are correct for each image opened in Icy.
Edit the metadata if needed.
Assign the source/target images according to Table 2 in eC-CLEM.
Choose the transformation model to be 'Rigid'.
Choose the noise model to be 'Isotropic'.
Press the play button.
Add fiducial markers to each of the images.
Rotate the field of view of an image if it helps with finding the same area in both images by right-clicking and dragging the mouse cursor.
Use high contrast cellular features such as nuclei or lipid droplets for fiducial markers.
Use extraneous features such as cracks in ice or foreign objects as fiducial markers.
Use features of the grid support film, such as holes and tears, as fiducial markers.
Place 2–3 points and compute the transform in ec-CLEM to reposition the image during transformation.
Open ec-CLEM in Icy.
Click advanced options and choose compute cascading transformation schema.
Add the transformation schema files (with suffix .transformation_schema.xml) for each image pair in the same order as shown in Table 2.
Add a Save location for the new 3D transformation schema file, ensuring you add .xml at the end of the filename you choose.
Press play to compute and save it.
Open the 3D image stacks corresponding to the aligned 2D SIR image (_SIR.dv or _SIR_ALN.dv if chromatic correction was performed) and the X-ray tomogram in Icy.
In the ec-CLEM advanced options, click Apply Transformation Schema.
Apply the new 3D schema to the SIR image stack.
Save the transformed image stack (Save As…).
Register the 3D stacks in the z direction.
Open the transformed SIR image stack and the 3D X-ray tomogram image stack in Icy.
Use ec-CLEM to add fiducial markers for 3D registration, keeping the RIGID option selected.
Lock both volumes using Lock 3 after adding fiducial markers.
Place between 5–10 points or until further improvement cannot be seen, using nanoparticles as fiducials.
Click stop once alignment is satisfactory.
Save the transformed image stacks and/or merged images.
Consider using the ‘SaveAsTifFast plugin’ for faster saving.
Generate an error map in ec-CLEM: After computing a transform, click Compute the whole predicted error map.
Adjust the histogram to scale the error map.
Toggle the appearance of the scale bar or color bar under ‘layer’ in the right bar shown in Icy.
Observe the maximum and minimum values on the color bar showing the values of the maximum and minimum error.
Install the histogram plugin in Icy.
Plot the error map distribution using the histogram plugin.
Measure the registration error between points used as landmarks by clicking on 'show measured error'.
Zoom in to the fiducial points to see red lines corresponding to error bars.
Use the ‘ruler helper’ tool in Icy to measure the length of each red line to obtain error magnitudes.
Create an image overlay of the tomogram on the SIR image using the Correlative View plugin.
Download the Correlative View plugin and save it in your Icy plugins folder.
Invert the transformation schema in ec-CLEM by going to Advanced→Invert schema.
Choose the final combined transformation schema you created previously.
Ensure that the schema has the file extension .xml, manually renaming if necessary.
Create a name for the new file, adding .xml at the end.
Click run to generate two new .xml output files.
Use the .xml output file with the suffix ‘matrixtransfo’ in the next step.
Open the maximum intensity SIR image in Icy.
Click the drop-down icon menu in the top-left of the image in Icy and find the Correlative View plugin.
Choose the minimum intensity tomogram image that you want to superimpose.
Choose the inverted transformation file that ends in ‘matrixtransfo’.
